title.orig: Sonnet 116: Let me not to the marriage of true minds
title.en: Sonnet 116: Let me not to the marriage of true minds
title.zh: 十四行诗第一百一十六首：我决不承认两颗真心的结合会有障碍

basis.en: Published in 1609 (Shakespeare’s Sonnets, Thomas Thorpe); the author died in 1616.
basis.zh: 1609 年出版（托马斯·索普印行的《莎士比亚十四行诗》）；作者卒于 1616 年。

note.en: Shakespeare defines love by what it is not: it does not alter, it does not bend, it is not Time’s fool. The central image is navigational, a fixed star whose height can be measured even when its worth cannot. The couplet stakes the whole of his writing on the claim, which is a bold way to end an argument.
note.zh: 莎士比亚用“爱不是什么”来定义爱：它不改变，不屈从，不做时间的弄臣。中心意象来自航海——一颗恒定的星，人们能测出它的高度，却测不出它的价值。最后两行把他的全部写作押在这个断言上，这是结束一场论证的大胆方式。

excerpt.orig:
It is the star to every wandering bark,
Whose worth’s unknown, although his height be taken.
excerpt.en:
It is the star to every wandering bark,
Whose worth’s unknown, although his height be taken.
excerpt.zh:
它是每一条漂泊之船所依的星，
高度可以测量，价值却无人知晓。
